question:
Consider the constraints $x+y\leq10$, $2x+y\leq14$, $x\geq0$ and $y\geq0$.
(i) Verify whether the points $P(2,6)$ and $Q(5,4)$ belong to the feasible region.
(ii) Determine whether either of these points lies on the boundary of the feasible region. Justify your answer.
explanation:
Step 1: Testing point $P(2,6)$
Substituting $x=2$ and $y=6$, we obtain $$2+6=8\leq10$$ and $$2(2)+6=10\leq14$$ Also, $2\geq0$ and $6\geq0$. Hence, $P(2,6)$ satisfies every constraint and belongs to the feasible region.
Step 2: Testing point $Q(5,4)$
For $Q(5,4)$, $$5+4=9\leq10$$ and $$2(5)+4=14\leq14$$ The non-negative restrictions are also satisfied. Therefore, $Q(5,4)$ is also feasible.
Step 3: Examining the boundary condition
At $P$, both principal inequalities are strict. At $Q$, $$2x+y=14$$ so $Q$ lies on the boundary line $2x+y=14$.
Step 4: Conclusion
Both $P$ and $Q$ belong to the feasible region, while $Q(5,4)$ lies on its boundary.

options.A:
(i) $P$ is feasible and $Q$ is infeasible
(ii) $P$ lies on $x+y=10$
options.B:
(i) Both $P$ and $Q$ are feasible
(ii) $P$ lies on the boundary and $Q$ is interior
options.C:
(i) Both $P$ and $Q$ are feasible
(ii) $Q$ lies on the boundary $2x+y=14$, while $P$ is interior
options.D:
(i) Both $P$ and $Q$ are infeasible
(ii) Neither lies on the boundary
